SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
MONDAY - SEPTEMBER 26, 2022 - 02:00 P.M.
CERRITOS LIBRARY, SKYLINE ROOM
18025 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the Cerritos Library Skyline Room will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting in-person in the Cerritos Library Skyline Room, subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 11:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 11:00 a.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL HELD MONDAY,
SEPTEMBER 26, 2022, 2:00 P.M., IN THE SKYLINE ROOM AT THE CERRITOS LIBRARY,
18025 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 2:05 p.m.

2.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Chuong Vo.

3.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem Bruce Barrows
  Mayor Chuong Vo

  Council Member Naresh Solanki was noted as absent from the Monday, September
  26, 2022, 2:00 p.m. City Council Special Meeting.

4.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos social media program (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Torrey Contreras, Senior Assistant City Manager, Bill Ihrke,
  City Attorney, Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer, Aaron Benjamin, Information
  Technology Manager, and Annie Hylton, City Librarian. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Murali Vasudevan submitted written correspondence requesting a social media policy,
  use of multiple social media platforms, and inquiring about the cost associated with
  agency social media use.

  Sue Carter submitted written correspondence expressing concerns regarding allowance
  of public comments on the City’s Facebook page.

  Gail Grossman submitted written correspondence expressing concerns regarding
  allowance of public comments on the City’s Facebook page.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Sam Desai spoke stating residents would prefer to communicate using a uniform
  platform, suggested replicating the social media programs used by cities listed in the
  agenda report, include use of the “NextDoor” platform, and requested the City schedule
  a community Town Hall meeting for further resident input.

  Murali Vasudevan thanked the Council and City staff for bringing this item back for
  review and suggested the City model its social media program on those presented in the
  agenda report.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 26, 2022, 2:00 p.m.
City Council Special Meeting  Page 2 of 2

4.  (continued)

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to provide the City Council with a
  memorandum that provides a summary update regarding the City’s social media sites
  which currently allow external “comments.”

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Direct the City Manager to provide an agenda report to the City Council regarding the
  City’s Social Media Program, which will include the following information:

  a. The goals of the City’s social media program;
  b. Descriptions of the platforms to be utilized, including Facebook Page, Facebook
  Group, Instagram, Twitter, and LinkedIn;
  c. A draft social media program policy, to include the appropriate disclaimers regarding
  public records and submission of legal notice, public records requests, and official
  written correspondence as listed in the agenda report;
  d. Description and estimated costs for an applicable social media management and
  archiving solution;
  e. Staff time and City resources required to support the social media program;
  f. Additional information relevant to the initiation of the expanded social media
  program; and

  2. Subsequent to City Council approval, launch the new program for a six to twelve-month
  trial period and schedule an agenda report for City Council review of the outcomes of the
  trial period (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Yokoyama, Barrows, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki
  ABSTAIN:  None

5.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 3:35 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk
